name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_STATEMENT3_Q01 - Endocrine ductless glands and scientific hormone definition

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Endocrine glands lack ducts and are hence called ductless glands.

Statement II: Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts.

Statement III: Invertebrates possess very complex endocrine systems with a far greater number of hormones than vertebrates.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the first proposition.
Endocrine glands release their secretions directly into extracellular fluids and circulation without ducts, which classifies them as ductless glands. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the second proposition.
The contemporary scientific definition explicitly defines hormones as non-nutrient chemicals functioning as intercellular messengers synthesized in minute, trace quantities. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the third proposition.
Invertebrates possess very simple endocrine systems with few hormones, whereas vertebrates possess a large number of chemicals providing endocrine coordination. Thus, this proposition is factually incorrect.

Step 4: Comparative synthesis.
The propositions regarding ductless glands and the scientific definition of hormones are correct, whereas the proposition claiming invertebrates have more complex endocrine systems than vertebrates is incorrect.

Final Answer: Statement I and Statement II only.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_STATEMENT3_Q02 - Hypothalamic diencephalon anatomy and dual pituitary regulation

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The hypothalamus forms the basal part of the diencephalon in the forebrain and contains neurosecretory nuclei.

Statement II: Hypothalamic releasing and inhibiting hormones reach the anterior pituitary through a portal circulatory system.

Statement III: The posterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the first proposition.
Anatomically, the hypothalamus resides at the base of the diencephalon in the forebrain and contains clusters of neurosecretory cells designated as nuclei. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the second proposition.
Regulatory neurohormones produced by hypothalamic neurons pass down axons, are released at nerve terminals, and travel via the hypophyseal portal circulation to control anterior pituitary secretions. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the third proposition.
The posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) is an anatomical extension of the brain and is under direct neural control, receiving hypothalamic hormones via direct axonal transport. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 4: Comparative synthesis.
All three propositions are correct because the hypothalamus forms the basal diencephalon with nuclei, controls the anterior pituitary via portal circulation, and regulates the posterior pituitary via direct neural innervation.

Final Answer: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_STATEMENT3_Q03 - Anterior pituitary trophic hormones and their targets

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland.

Statement II: Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) stimulates the synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex.

Statement III: Prolactin stimulates Leydig cells in the male testis to synthesize and secrete androgens.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the first proposition.
TSH secreted by the pars distalis acts on follicular cells of the thyroid gland to trigger thyroid hormone synthesis and release. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the second proposition.
ACTH stimulates the adrenal cortex to synthesize and release steroid corticoids, primarily glucocorticoids like cortisol. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the third proposition.
It is luteinizing hormone (LH), not prolactin, that stimulates Leydig cells to produce androgens; prolactin regulates mammary gland growth and milk synthesis. Thus, this proposition is factually incorrect.

Step 4: Comparative synthesis.
The propositions regarding TSH and ACTH actions are correct, whereas the proposition attributing androgen secretion to prolactin is incorrect because that function is mediated by luteinizing hormone.

Final Answer: Statement I and Statement II only.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_STATEMENT3_Q04 - Gonadotrophic regulation of testicular and ovarian cycles

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: In human males, luteinizing hormone (LH) stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens from the testis.

Statement II: In human females, LH induces ovulation of fully mature graafian follicles and maintains the corpus luteum.

Statement III: In human males, follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) and androgens jointly regulate the process of spermatogenesis.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the first proposition.
LH binds to interstitial Leydig cells in the testis, stimulating the production of testosterone and other androgens. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the second proposition.
The mid-cycle LH surge triggers ovulation of the mature Graafian follicle and supports the subsequent maintenance of the endocrine corpus luteum. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the third proposition.
Spermatogenesis requires the synergistic actions of FSH on Sertoli cells and testosterone from Leydig cells within the seminiferous tubules. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 4: Comparative synthesis.
All three propositions are correct because LH regulates Leydig cell androgen production in males and ovulation/corpus luteum maintenance in females, while FSH and androgens jointly govern spermatogenesis.

Final Answer: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_STATEMENT3_Q05 - Pineal gland location and circadian regulation by melatonin

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The pineal gland is an endocrine structure located on the dorsal side of the forebrain.

Statement II: Melatonin is an enzyme that destroys melanocytes to eliminate skin pigmentation.

Statement III: Melatonin plays a critical role in the regulation of the 24-hour diurnal rhythm of our sleep-wake cycle and body temperature.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the first proposition.
The pineal gland is situated anatomically on the dorsal aspect of the forebrain. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the second proposition.
Melatonin is a hormone (not an enzyme) that influences pigmentation without destroying melanocytes. Thus, this proposition is factually incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the third proposition.
Melatonin acts on circadian pacemakers to coordinate diurnal rhythms, including sleep-wake periodicity and core body temperature fluctuations. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 4: Comparative synthesis.
The propositions regarding the anatomical position of the pineal gland and the diurnal regulatory role of melatonin are correct, while the proposition describing melatonin as a destructive enzyme is incorrect.

Final Answer: Statement I and Statement III only.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_STATEMENT3_Q06 - Thyroid anatomy and endocrine control over metabolism

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The human thyroid gland consists of five distinct lobes embedded deep within the thoracic mediastinum.

Statement II: Thyroid follicular cells synthesize two hormones: tetraiodothyronine (thyroxine) and triiodothyronine.

Statement III: Thyroid hormones play a major role in the regulation of the basal metabolic rate and support erythropoiesis.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the first proposition.
The thyroid gland consists of two lateral lobes situated in the neck on either side of the trachea, not five lobes in the mediastinum. Thus, this proposition is factually incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of the second proposition.
The thyroid follicles are lined with follicular cells that synthesize tetraiodothyronine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3). Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the third proposition.
Thyroid hormones control basal metabolic rate, macromolecule metabolism, water-electrolyte balance, and support red blood cell formation. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 4: Comparative synthesis.
The propositions regarding thyroid hormone synthesis by follicular cells and their metabolic/erythropoietic roles are correct, whereas the anatomical proposition asserting five mediastinal lobes is incorrect.

Final Answer: Statement II and Statement III only.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_STATEMENT3_Q07 - Antagonistic calcium regulation by parathyroid and thyrocalcitonin

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) is a hypercalcemic hormone that increases blood \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) levels by stimulating bone resorption.

Statement II: PTH decreases blood calcium concentration by promoting massive calcium excretion through renal filtration.

Statement III: PTH and thyrocalcitonin (TCT) act antagonistically to play a significant role in calcium balance in the body.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the first proposition.
PTH stimulates osteoclastic bone resorption (demineralization), releasing calcium into the bloodstream and elevating blood calcium. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the second proposition.
PTH stimulates the reabsorption of calcium by renal tubules, thereby conserving calcium rather than promoting its excretion. Thus, this proposition is factually incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the third proposition.
PTH elevates blood calcium levels (hypercalcemic), while TCT secreted by the thyroid gland decreases blood calcium levels (hypocalcemic), jointly maintaining calcium homeostasis. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 4: Comparative synthesis.
The propositions regarding PTH elevating blood calcium via bone resorption and the antagonistic relationship between PTH and TCT are correct, while the proposition claiming PTH lowers calcium via renal excretion is incorrect.

Final Answer: Statement I and Statement III only.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_STATEMENT3_Q08 - Thymus anatomy and dual adaptive immune functions

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The thymus gland is a lobular structure located between the lungs behind the sternum on the ventral side of the aorta.

Statement II: Thymosins play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes, which provide cell-mediated immunity.

Statement III: Thymosins promote the production of antibodies to provide humoral immunity.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the first proposition.
Anatomically, the thymus is positioned in the mediastinum between the lungs, situated retrosternally on the ventral aspect of the aorta. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the second proposition.
The peptide hormones called thymosins drive the maturation and clonal differentiation of T-lymphocytes, providing cell-mediated immunity. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the third proposition.
In addition to cell-mediated differentiation, thymosins also augment antibody production by B-lymphocytes, conferring humoral immunity. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 4: Comparative synthesis.
All three propositions are correct because the thymus is located behind the sternum on the ventral side of the aorta and produces thymosins that promote both cell-mediated and humoral immunity.

Final Answer: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_STATEMENT3_Q09 - Adrenal medullary catecholamine secretions during fight flight

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The adrenal medulla secretes mineralocorticoids like aldosterone in response to acute stress.

Statement II: Adrenaline and noradrenaline increase alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection, and sweating.

Statement III: Both catecholamines increase the heart beat, strength of cardiac contraction, and rate of respiration.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the first proposition.
Mineralocorticoids like aldosterone are secreted by the outer adrenal cortex (zona glomerulosa), whereas the medulla secretes catecholamines. Thus, this proposition is factually incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of the second proposition.
Catecholamines rapidly prepare the organism for fight-or-flight emergencies by enhancing sensory alertness, causing pupil dilation, piloerection, and diaphoresis. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the third proposition.
Adrenaline and noradrenaline stimulate beta-adrenergic cardiac receptors and respiratory centers, elevating heart rate, myocardial contractility, and ventilation rate. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 4: Comparative synthesis.
The propositions detailing catecholamine-mediated sympathetic arousal and cardiovascular stimulation are correct, whereas the proposition attributing mineralocorticoid secretion to the medulla is incorrect.

Final Answer: Statement II and Statement III only.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_STATEMENT3_Q10 - Adrenal cortex histological zonation and cortisol metabolism

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The adrenal cortex is divided into three layers: zona reticularis (inner), zona fasciculata (middle), and zona glomerulosa (outer).

Statement II: Glucocorticoids, particularly cortisol, stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, and proteolysis, and inhibit cellular amino acid uptake.

Statement III: Aldosterone acts at the renal tubules to stimulate the reabsorption of \(\text{K}^+\) and excretion of \(\text{Na}^+\).

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the first proposition.
From inner to outer, the adrenal cortical zones are zona reticularis, zona fasciculata, and zona glomerulosa. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the second proposition.
Cortisol promotes hepatic gluconeogenesis and macromolecule catabolism (lipolysis and proteolysis), while decreasing amino acid uptake by peripheral cells. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the third proposition.
Aldosterone stimulates the reabsorption of Na+ and water, and stimulates the excretion of K+ and phosphate ions, the reverse of what is stated. Thus, this proposition is factually incorrect.

Step 4: Comparative synthesis.
The propositions regarding cortical layer organization and cortisol's catabolic/gluconeogenic metabolic effects are correct, whereas the proposition regarding aldosterone ion transport is incorrect.

Final Answer: Statement I and Statement II only.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_STATEMENT3_Q11 - Endocrine pancreatic islets and cellular glucose regulation

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The Islets of Langerhans constitute approximately 80 to 90 percent of the total pancreatic tissue mass.

Statement II: The two main types of endocrine cells in the Islet of Langerhans are \(\alpha\)-cells (secreting glucagon) and \(\beta\)-cells (secreting insulin).

Statement III: Insulin acts on hepatocytes and adipocytes to enhance cellular glucose uptake, resulting in hypoglycemia.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the first proposition.
The Islets of Langerhans number about 1 to 2 million and represent only 1 to 2 percent of total pancreatic tissue, the remainder being exocrine acini. Thus, this proposition is factually incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of the second proposition.
The endocrine islets consist primarily of alpha-cells that produce glucagon and beta-cells that produce insulin. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the third proposition.
Insulin promotes the translocation of glucose into liver and adipose cells, stimulating glycogenesis and lowering circulating blood glucose levels. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 4: Comparative synthesis.
The propositions identifying islet cell types and insulin's hypoglycemic mechanism are correct, whereas the proposition overestimating the islet mass as 80 to 90 percent is incorrect.

Final Answer: Statement II and Statement III only.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_STATEMENT3_Q12 - Secretory actions of gastrointestinal peptide regulatory hormones

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Gastrin acts on gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen.

Statement II: Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates the secretion of water and bicarbonate ions.

Statement III: Cholecystokinin (CCK) acts on both the pancreas and gall bladder, stimulating pancreatic enzymes and bile juice secretion.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the first proposition.
Gastrin released by gastric mucosal cells acts on parietal and chief cells to stimulate hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen secretion. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the second proposition.
Secretin stimulates ductal cells in the exocrine pancreas to secrete watery bicarbonate-rich fluid that neutralizes duodenal chyme. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the third proposition.
CCK stimulates gall bladder contraction to discharge bile juice and acinar cells of the pancreas to release digestive enzymes. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 4: Comparative synthesis.
All three propositions are correct because gastrin stimulates gastric HCl/pepsinogen, secretin stimulates pancreatic water/bicarbonate, and CCK stimulates gallbladder bile release and pancreatic enzyme secretion.

Final Answer: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_STATEMENT3_Q13 - Endocrine peptides of the atrium and juxtaglomerular apparatus

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The atrial wall of the human heart secretes atrial natriuretic factor (ANF) when blood pressure is increased.

Statement II: ANF causes dilation of blood vessels, thereby reducing blood pressure.

Statement III: The juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney produce erythropoietin, which stimulates the formation of red blood cells.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the first proposition.
Atrial distension resulting from high blood volume or blood pressure stimulates atrial myocytes to secrete the peptide hormone ANF. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the second proposition.
ANF causes relaxation of vascular smooth muscle (vasodilation), decreasing systemic vascular resistance and lowering blood pressure. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the third proposition.
Specialized juxtaglomerular cells of the renal cortex synthesize and release erythropoietin, which stimulates erythroid differentiation in bone marrow. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 4: Comparative synthesis.
All three propositions are correct because ANF is secreted during elevated blood pressure to cause vasodilation, and juxtaglomerular cells produce erythropoietin to stimulate erythropoiesis.

Final Answer: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHEMICAL_COORDINATION_AND_INTEGRATION_STATEMENT3_Q14 - Membrane bound second messengers versus intracellular genomic signaling

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Hormones interacting with membrane-bound receptors generate second messengers like cyclic AMP, \(\text{IP}_3\), or \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) to regulate cellular metabolism.

Statement II: Lipid-soluble steroid hormones and iodothyronines interact with intracellular receptors to regulate gene expression or chromosome function.

Statement III: Hormone receptors show broad cross-reactivity and bind indiscriminately to any circulating steroid or peptide hormone.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the first proposition.
Peptide and protein hormones bind to cell-surface receptors, generating intracellular second messengers (cAMP, IP3, Ca2+) that activate enzymatic pathways without the hormone entering the cell. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the second proposition.
Steroid hormones and thyroid hormones cross the plasma membrane and bind to intracellular/nuclear receptors, interacting directly with genomic DNA to regulate transcription. Thus, this proposition is scientifically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the third proposition.
Hormone receptors exhibit strict ligand specificity; each receptor is uniquely shaped to bind only one specific hormone. Thus, this proposition is factually incorrect.

Step 4: Comparative synthesis.
The propositions detailing membrane receptor second-messenger signaling and intracellular receptor genomic regulation are correct, whereas the proposition claiming indiscriminate receptor binding is incorrect because receptors are strictly specific.

Final Answer: Statement I and Statement II only.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III
